title: DoT
team: Myeongseong Kim, Woohun Lee, Andrea Bianchi
summary: DoT is a tabletop mixed-reality game platform that brings a physical marble into a digital game.
Players touch and move the marble on a display, while the system moves it in sync with on-screen graphics.

paragraph: DoT is a tabletop mixed-reality game platform in which a steel marble serves as both a game controller and a moving game piece.
Players interact with the game by touching and moving the marble directly on a display.
The system responds through on-screen graphics and the marble's physical movement, connecting digital gameplay with an object players can hold and manipulate.
Beneath the display, a motorized two-axis mechanism carries a magnet that guides the steel marble across the screen.
When a player touches the conductive marble, the capacitive touch panel detects the contact and the marble's position.
Together, touch sensing and magnetic actuation allow the same object to receive player input and provide physical feedback.
Developed through Interactive Product Design (Spring 2018, instructor: Prof. Woohun Lee) and Graduation Design Studio II (Fall 2018, advisor: Prof. Andrea Bianchi).
